title: Delete liquid cooling and revert to passive conduction into a finned housing, using a 75 degC-capable cell

ideaData.title: Delete liquid cooling and revert to passive conduction into a finned housing, using a 75 degC-capable cell
ideaData.studyDecisionReason: Selected. No conflict with any other selected idea and it won its position in the conflict graph.
ideaData.groups: E Housing and closure, F Thermal and coolant
ideaData.componentsAffected: Housing, A380 die casting; Coolant port fitting; Coolant port seal; Coolant port retention clip; Coolant gallery core plug; Coolant charge, glycol; Thermal conductive adhesive
ideaData.targetFunctions: Transfer heat; Support mass; Contain liquid; Exclude water; Transfer load; Contain debris; Convey liquid; Prevent leakage; Control position; Transmit force
ideaData.technicalDescription: Remove the cast jacket, both coolant ports, their seals and retention clips, the two gallery core plugs and the factory glycol charge. Add external cast fins to the housing side walls and reduce the adhesive to a controlled thin bond line. The enabling change is at the cell, not the housing: Bosch developed cells for its 48V pack that deliver full output at temperatures up to 75 degC without any reduction in service life, and cools passively by exploiting the thermal conductivity of heat sinks in the immediate vicinity of the installed position. Combine with a higher-conductivity alloy — Castasil-37 at up to 173 W/m.K against A380's 96 to 98 — so the fins do more with less section.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Cost leaves in five places at once. Inside the boundary: the cored jacket goes, taking the cores, the drilled access, the two plugs at £0.70 and the vacuum impregnation at £1.20 with it; the coolant interface parts go at £2.74; the glycol charge goes at £0.18; and the adhesive falls because the bond line no longer has to serve a gallery. Outside the boundary: the leak test leaves the end-of-line cascade, and the vehicle's hoses, its share of the pump and the associated control all go, reported on a separate cross-boundary line that is never added to the pack figure. Stage 2 puts the thermal decision at £15.49, 6.4 per cent of the bill of materials, across Transfer heat, Contain liquid, Convey liquid and Dissipate heat. The functions this idea targets carry a combined value gap of £12.84 at Stage 3, against an affected component cost of £26.61; the saving claimed here is capped at that gap when the register is totalled.
ideaData.riskNotes: This idea stands or falls on one question the study cannot answer: why the pack is liquid cooled at all. If the driver is sustained power on a hot-country towing duty cycle, passive cooling is not available and the idea is void. If it is coolant-circuit commonality with the power electronics, it is nearly free. A 75 degC-capable cell also costs more per kWh than a 55 degC-capable one, so part of the saving returns at the largest line. It conflicts directly with integrating the DC-DC converter, which dissipates continuously where a BMS does not.
ideaData.validationRequired: Pack thermal model at 45 degC ambient on the hot-country towing duty cycle, then a hardware soak test against DO-05's 55 degC limit and 5 degC spread. Cell supplier confirmation of full output to 75 degC without service-life reduction, and the price of that cell against the current one. Confirmation from the programme of the original reason for liquid cooling before any of this is worth running.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Bosch 48V pack: cells developed to deliver full output up to 75 degC without any reduction in service life; passive cooling exploiting the thermal conductivity of heat sinks in the immediate vicinity of the installed position; plastic housing (automotive-iq.com, 23 Aug 2024; chargedevs.com, 6 Nov 2017). A123 48V pack: no active cooling below 25 degC (US EPA, SAE 2018-01-0433). MAHLE Powertrain 48V pack: a high efficiency yet simple cooling system holding cells under 55 degC, with the busbar designed to prevent additional heat input into the cell terminals (mahle-powertrain.com). Castasil-37 at up to 173 W/m.K (EMP Tech, Sep 2026).
ideaData.investmentText: New casting die, of the order of 180k GBP; the leak test station is deleted.
ideaData.savingBasis: part-specific band, deep-dive
ideaData.nreNote: Carries the full investment for this asset.

ideaData.reviewOpenPoints: [MAJOR · quality] The saving band is not derived from the stated mechanism. The itemised deletions total about £4.8 (plugs £0.70, impregnation £1.20, port parts £2.74, glycol £0.18), plus some adhesive. Reaching £11.18-£17.03 needs a £4-£10 fall in the £19.21 casting, while fins and a dearer alloy are added and a dearer 75 degC cell returns 'part of the saving at the largest line'. That penalty is not netted. The high saving (£17.03) also exceeds the £12.84 value-gap cap the text itself states. Evidence: Mechanism: 'two plugs at £0.70 and the vacuum impregnation at £1.20 ... coolant interface parts go at £2.74; the glycol charge goes at £0.18'. Risk: 'A 75 degC-capable cell also costs more per kWh ... part of the saving returns at the largest line.' Value gap £12.84. Recommendation: Present it as an architecture decision (deck Decision 1, 'confirm why the pack is liquid cooled'), not as a quoted saving. ¶ [MAJOR · quality] Double-counting between two Develop ideas. ID-001 'reduce[s] the adhesive to a controlled thin bond line', and ID-011 (Develop) cuts the same £3.78 adhesive. Both also claim the housing. They share no conflict set (ID-001: C1, C27-31; ID-011: C19), so the development list counts the adhesive saving twice. Evidence: ID-001 Specifics: 'reduce the adhesive to a controlled thin bond line'; ID-011: 'cut the thermal interface material volume'. Both list 'Thermal conductive adhesive; Housing, A380 die casting'. Recommendation: Add a conflict edge, or net the overlap. Report to the author. ¶ [MINOR · consistency] The text and the conflict map disagree. ID-001 says it 'conflicts directly with integrating the DC-DC converter' (ID-003), and ID-003 says 'The two radical ideas are in direct conflict'. But no conflict set contains both: ID-001 is in C1 and C27-C31, ID-003 is in C11. Evidence: Conflicts sheet: C1 = ID-001, ID-010, ID-146, ID-128, ID-117, ID-113, ID-119, ID-120; C11 = ID-009, ID-003, ID-131, ID-062, ID-058. Recommendation: Flag to the author. No effect on decisions, because ID-003 is Not selected. ¶ [MINOR · quality] Weighted score 3.47 is below the 3.95 threshold. The selection is defensible through the 1%-of-BOM material route (risk-adjusted high above £2.42), but the recorded reason cites only 'won its position in the conflict graph'. Evidence: Evaluation ID-001: Weighted 3.47. Recommendation: Make the reason state the material-saving route. ¶ [MINOR · benchmark] Benchmark claim not found: Bosch cells deliver FULL output to 75 degC 'without any reduction in service life'. Sources confirm operation to 75 degC and 'long lifetime even at high operating temperature', but no source states full output or zero life reduction. The Bosch pack is also much smaller than this study's (360 Wh, 14 kW peak, under 6 kg in plastic, against 836 Wh, 12 kg), which weakens the read-across to a pack whose cooling has to handle a hot-country towing case. Evidence: https://www.delo-adhesives.com/press-and-news/delo-news/details/bosch-relies-on-delo-adhesives-for-mild-hybrid-systems Recommendation: Show the claim as unverified, or correct it, before the Director presentation. ¶ [MINOR · benchmark] Benchmark claim not found: Castasil-37 thermal conductivity up to 173 W/m.K (EMP Tech, Sep 2026). No source found for the figure. Check it against the Rheinfelden datasheet. Evidence: none: WebSearch for Castasil-37 thermal conductivity returned no source naming the alloy Recommendation: Show the claim as unverified, or correct it, before the Director presentation.

title: Move the cell compression duty into the housing and delete the module frame

ideaData.title: Move the cell compression duty into the housing and delete the module frame
ideaData.studyDecisionReason: Mutually exclusive with a higher scoring idea already selected: ID-006.
ideaData.groups: B Module frame, E Housing and closure
ideaData.componentsAffected: Housing, A380 die casting; Top cover, PA66 GF30; Module side plate; Module end plate; Module tie rod; Tie rod nut; Module frame fastener; Stack side compliance foam
ideaData.targetFunctions: Support mass; Transfer heat; Contain liquid; Exclude water; Contain debris; Apply force; Transfer load; Restrain movement; Resist vibration; Prevent contact; Absorb expansion; Permit access; Transmit force; Damp movement
ideaData.technicalDescription: Design the housing and cover so that the enclosure itself reacts cell expansion, as Bosch does with a plastic 48V housing. Delete both side plates, both end plates, both tie rods and nuts, the frame fasteners and the side compliance foam. Cells are located and preloaded by moulded or cast features and a single compliance layer.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Eight part numbers collapse into features on two parts that already exist. Assembly cycle falls because the module sub-assembly step disappears entirely; the stack is built directly into the housing. Tooling cost rises on the housing and cover, which is charged against the saving. The functions this idea targets carry a combined value gap of £14.65 at Stage 3, against an affected component cost of £29.48; the saving claimed here is capped at that gap when the register is totalled.
ideaData.riskNotes: The housing now carries a fourth duty on top of structure, heat path and coolant containment, and creep under sustained preload becomes a design case for a moulded part. Service becomes harder: a cell fault means scrapping more of the assembly. Preload repeatability at end of life is the technical risk.
ideaData.validationRequired: Creep and stress relaxation test on the housing material at 85 degC over programme life, then cell preload measurement at beginning and end of life against the cell supplier's window.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Bosch 48V pack: plastic housing that protects against external damage while withstanding the continual expansion and contraction of the cells through service life (automotive-iq.com, 23 Aug 2024).
ideaData.investmentText: Housing and cover tooling change, of the order of 200k GBP combined.

title: Integrate the 48V-to-12V DC-DC converter into the pack

ideaData.title: Integrate the 48V-to-12V DC-DC converter into the pack
ideaData.studyDecisionReason: Mutually exclusive with a higher scoring idea already selected: ID-062.
ideaData.componentsAffected: BMS printed circuit assembly; Signal connector; Internal sense harness; BMS board-to-wire connector
ideaData.targetFunctions: Monitor voltage; Balance voltage; Transmit data; Exclude moisture; Sense temperature; Measure current; Transfer current
ideaData.technicalDescription: Bring the DC-DC converter inside the pack housing and share the board, the housing, the thermal path, the connector set and the communication interface with the BMS, as Hella does in its 48V PowerPack.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: One enclosure, one thermal interface, one set of external connectors and one wiring interface replace two. The saving inside our boundary is on the shared board and connector content; the larger saving is the converter's own housing, connectors and mounting, which sits outside the boundary and is reported on a separate line that is never added to the pack saving. The functions this idea targets carry a combined value gap of £25.63 at Stage 3, against an affected component cost of £43.20; the saving claimed here is capped at that gap when the register is totalled.
ideaData.riskNotes: The pack becomes a thermal problem: a DC-DC converter dissipates continuously where the BMS does not, which pushes back against deleting the cooling. The two radical ideas are in direct conflict. Pack mass and volume rise, and a converter fault now means replacing the battery.
ideaData.validationRequired: Thermal co-simulation of converter and cells in one enclosure, and an ASIL decomposition covering both functions on shared hardware.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Hella 48V PowerPack: a 48V lithium block combining the battery with the battery management and the DC/DC converter, done to reduce engineering cost and optimise packaging (automotive-iq.com, 23 Aug 2024).
ideaData.investmentText: New board, new housing provision, functional safety rework. NRE of the order of 1.5m GBP.

title: Change chemistry to LFP at 14S1P and hand the cold-crank case to a preheat or a 12V assist

ideaData.title: Change chemistry to LFP at 14S1P and hand the cold-crank case to a preheat or a 12V assist
ideaData.studyDecisionReason: Selected. No conflict with any other selected idea and it won its position in the conflict graph.
ideaData.componentsAffected: NMC prismatic cell; Cell-to-cell propagation barrier; Cell-to-cell insulation film
ideaData.targetFunctions: Store energy; Deliver power; Accept charge; Deliver current; Block heat; Resist voltage
ideaData.technicalDescription: Replace 12S1P 19 Ah NMC with 14S1P LFP at equal energy: 14 cells at 3.2 V nominal gives 44.8 V, inside the 48V class at 3.65 V per cell maximum, which 14S NMC would not be at 4.2 V. China LFP cell price is 55 to 65 USD/kWh against 85 to 95 for NMC. Because LFP's temperature rise rate in nail penetration is around a hundred times lower than NMC's, the 1.0 mm mica barrier at £6.05 can be reduced to a plain film or deleted, and the venting duty falls with it. The A123 14S1P LFP pouch pack characterised by the US EPA is the documented architecture.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Two lines move together. The cell falls from a base of about 90 USD/kWh to about 60, a 33 per cent material reduction before the power premium is re-set; LFP needs a higher overbuild for the same power, taken at 2.4 times against NMC's 2.2, so the net cell reduction is about 27 per cent, roughly £33 on £122.41. The barrier falls by up to £6.05 because the abuse case it exists for is far milder. Two extra cells add two busbars, two sense channels and two insulation films, about £1.20, charged against the saving. The functions this idea targets carry a combined value gap of £41.69 at Stage 3, against an affected component cost of £129.12; the saving claimed here is capped at that gap when the register is totalled.
ideaData.riskNotes: LFP cannot deliver DO-04, 30 A for 10 seconds at minus 30 degC and 50 per cent state of charge, without one of three answers: a larger cell, a cell preheat, or handing cranking back to a 12V battery — and the third directly contradicts the register's own idea of deleting the 12V battery. LFP energy density is lower, so the pack grows in volume and mass against a 12 kg figure the model already overshoots by 0.876 kg. The 14S string also voids the 12S monitoring device idea unless the pin-compatible 14S part is used instead.
ideaData.validationRequired: Cold-crank pulse test at minus 30 degC and 50 per cent state of charge on a specific candidate LFP cell, to DO-04's 30 A for 10 seconds. Nail penetration or equivalent propagation test to establish whether the mica barrier can be downgraded, and by how much. Volumetric and mass study against the existing envelope. Charge acceptance at minus 10 degC for the regen case in DO-03.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: A123 Systems 48V MHEV pack: 14S1P LFP pouch, 8 Ah, 0.4 kWh, characterised by the US EPA at NVFEL on regulatory drive cycles, with no active cooling below 25 degC (SAE 2018-01-0433). LFP exhibits roughly a 100 times lower temperature rise rate than NMC in nail penetration abuse testing (PatSnap, 9 Apr 2026). China LFP cell 55 to 65 USD/kWh against NMC 85 to 95 (BAKTH Battery, 15 Jun 2026).
ideaData.investmentText: Cell requalification, busbar and contacting system tooling, of the order of 450k GBP.
ideaData.savingBasis: part-specific band, deep-dive
ideaData.nreNote: Marginal share only. The full Moulding tooling investment is carried by ID-064; summing full NRE on every idea would overstate investment badly.

ID-064: nreGBP 30000, investmentText 'Panel tooling.' Deck slide 12 'Cost to do £90,000; Payback 0.05 years'. Recommendation: Show £450k as the investment, or flag the NRE as under review. ¶ [MAJOR · quality] There is an unrecorded conflict with ID-059, the Develop 12S front end (see the ID-059 finding). The high saving also exceeds the stated arithmetic: the cell (about £33) plus the barrier (up to £6.05) less the added parts (£1.20) is about £37.9, against a claimed high of £43.90, which is above the £41.69 value-gap cap. ideaData.studyDecisionReason: Mutually exclusive with a higher scoring idea already selected: ID-004.
ideaData.componentsAffected: NMC prismatic cell; Cell-to-cell propagation barrier
ideaData.targetFunctions: Store energy; Deliver power; Accept charge; Deliver current; Block heat
ideaData.technicalDescription: Replace the NMC string with automotive sodium-ion cells. CATL states its Naxtra passenger cell operates from minus 40 to plus 70 degC and retains 90 per cent usable power at the low extreme, at 175 Wh/kg and more than 10,000 cycles, and that it has passed China's GB 38031-2025 traction battery safety standard effective 1 July 2026. Sodium cells can use aluminium rather than copper as the anode current collector, which removes copper foil from the cell's own bill of materials. Sodium-ion start-stop products are already offered in 12V, 24V and 48V.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: The power premium is the mechanism, not the cell price. Our cell is bought at about 2.2 times an energy-cell price because DO-04 requires 30 A for 10 seconds at minus 30 degC, and cold power is what sizes it. If the chemistry delivers cold power inherently, the premium collapses toward an energy-cell basis, and the premium multiplies 50.5 per cent of the bill of materials. A drop from 2.2 to 1.5 times on a 90 USD/kWh base is 198 to 135 USD/kWh, about £39 on the cell line. The aluminium anode collector is a second, smaller reduction inside the cell. The functions this idea targets carry a combined value gap of £41.69 at Stage 3, against an affected component cost of £128.46; the saving claimed here is capped at that gap when the register is totalled.
ideaData.riskNotes: The evidence cuts both ways and this is a genuine gamble. A 2026 starter-battery study found a sodium pack performed well at moderate temperatures and at minus 5 degC when charged to the correct voltage, but failed to sustain the required pulses at minus 15 degC, and attributed it to electrolyte, interface and transport limitations requiring better chemistry, preheating or improved system control. Low temperature performance is a design achievement of a specific cell, not a property of the chemistry. Sodium-ion at 175 Wh/kg is also below NMC, so the pack grows against a 12 kg target already overshot.
ideaData.validationRequired: Cold-crank pulse test at minus 30 degC and 50 per cent state of charge on the specific candidate cell, not on the chemistry, to DO-04. Cycle life against DO-06 at the pack duty cycle. Volumetric and mass study at 175 Wh/kg. Over-discharge behaviour check, since an aluminium anode collector changes it.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: CATL Naxtra: minus 40 to plus 70 degC, 90 per cent usable power retained at the low extreme, 175 Wh/kg, over 10,000 cycles, GB 38031-2025 passed; aluminium usable as anode current collector (GlobalSpec, 19 Feb 2026). Sodium-ion start-stop batteries offered at 12V, 24V and 48V, 10 to 200 Ah (Tycorun). Counter-evidence: a 2026 starter-battery study found failure to sustain required pulses at minus 15 degC (lokithor.net, 29 Jul 2026).
ideaData.investmentText: Full cell qualification programme, of the order of 800k GBP.

title: Cell-to-pack construction, deleting the module as an intermediate level

ideaData.studyDecisionReason: Selected. No conflict with any other selected idea and it won its position in the conflict graph.

ideaData.targetFunctions: Store energy; Deliver power; Accept charge; Deliver current; Conduct current; Apply force; Restrain movement; Resist voltage; Resist vibration; Absorb expansion; Prevent contact; Control spacing
ideaData.technicalDescription: Assemble cells directly into the housing with no module frame, no stack cover and a simplified interconnect laid straight onto the cell tops, following the documented cell-to-pack architecture generation used on traction packs.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: A whole level of the product structure disappears. Parts, interfaces, assembly steps and the tolerance stack between module and housing all go. ideaData.validationRequired: Tolerance stack study from cell to housing, and a vibration test of cells retained by housing features rather than by a steel frame.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Cell-to-pack and cell-to-body are documented architecture generations; electrode-to-pack has been demonstrated by 24M (batterydesign.net). No published 48V cell-to-pack benchmark was found, and on twelve cells the case is weaker than on a traction pack.

title: Move the interconnect from Cu-ETP to nickel-plated EN AW-1050A aluminium at 1.64 times section, welded ultrasonically

ideaData.title: Move the interconnect from Cu-ETP to nickel-plated EN AW-1050A aluminium at 1.64 times section, welded ultrasonically
ideaData.studyDecisionReason: Mutually exclusive with a higher scoring idea already selected: ID-006.
ideaData.componentsAffected: Cell interconnect busbar, Cu T2Y; Flexible copper busbar, Cu T2Y2; Sealing stud terminal, Cu T2Y; Busbar terminal bolt
ideaData.targetFunctions: Conduct current; Transfer current; Absorb expansion; Prevent leakage; Transmit force
ideaData.technicalDescription: Replace Cu T2Y and Cu T2Y2 with EN AW-1050A or 1350 aluminium busbars, nickel-plated at the joint areas only. Aluminium's conductivity is about 61 per cent IACS against copper's 100, so conductance parity needs 1.64 times the cross-sectional area: on a 300 A pack a 3 mm copper bar becomes about 5 mm of aluminium. Change the joining process at the same time, from laser welding to ultrasonic welding, which does not melt the metal and therefore both tolerates aluminium's oxide film and removes the weld-penetration risk to the cell terminal.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Copper stood at 14,440 USD/t on 4 September 2026 against an IMF LME spot average for 2026 of 12,842, so this content is priced at the top of its own year. Aluminium busbar stock at roughly 2,000 to 2,400 USD/t is about one seventh of that. At 1.64 times the section but 30 per cent of copper's density, the aluminium bar weighs about half as much for equal current rating, so the material cost falls to roughly a tenth. Across the thirteen busbars, the flexible busbar, both terminal studs and the take-off bolts the copper material content is about £8.00 of the £12.15 group, and roughly £7.20 of that leaves. Plating cost partly returns, which is why the band is not larger. The functions this idea targets carry a combined value gap of £5.16 at Stage 3, against an affected component cost of £10.49; the saving claimed here is capped at that gap when the register is totalled.
ideaData.riskNotes: Aluminium forms a natural oxide that raises joint resistance if it is not managed, and laser welding aluminium to a nickel-plated copper or steel cell terminal is a dissimilar-metal joint with intermetallic formation, large differences in melting point, thermal conductivity and expansion coefficient, and an active research literature rather than a settled process. Ultrasonic welding solves the metallurgy but applies mechanical load to a prismatic cell terminal and limits joint area by sonotrode size, and 26 joints per pack may take longer than laser. The 1.64 times section also costs packaging height above the cell tops, competing with the busbar cover and the top cover.
ideaData.validationRequired: Joint resistance and temperature rise across thermal cycling on the actual cell terminal material, not on a coupon. Dissimilar-weld process capability study with cross-section metallography for intermetallic thickness. Cell terminal load measurement during ultrasonic welding. Packaging check of the taller busbar against the cover. Salt spray on the selectively plated joint.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Aluminium costs less and weighs about half as much as copper at equal current rating, needing about 5 mm where copper needs 3 mm on a 300 A pack; the oxide layer raises joint resistance if unmanaged, and ultrasonic welding, which does not melt the metal, pairs well with aluminium. Nickel-plated copper remains the most common lithium-pack choice because nickel resists corrosion and holds stable resistance across thousands of thermal cycles (SunLith Energy, 15 Jul 2026). Laser weld depth control is critical because excessive penetration can damage the cell (Joining Technologies). Al-to-steel and Al-to-Cu laser joints show large thermo-physical mismatch and are an active research problem (ScienceDirect, 10 Mar 2022; AIMS Materials Science, 2022).

title: Move the coolant boundary out of the HPDC casting into a stamped and vacuum-brazed 3003 aluminium cold plate

ideaData.title: Move the coolant boundary out of the HPDC casting into a stamped and vacuum-brazed 3003 aluminium cold plate
ideaData.studyDecisionReason: Mutually exclusive with a higher scoring idea already selected: ID-001.
ideaData.groups: E Housing and closure, F Thermal and coolant
ideaData.componentsAffected: Coolant port fitting; Coolant port seal; Coolant port retention clip; Coolant gallery core plug; Housing, A380 die casting
ideaData.targetFunctions: Support mass; Transfer heat; Contain liquid; Exclude water; Transfer load; Contain debris; Convey liquid; Prevent leakage; Transmit force
ideaData.technicalDescription: Delete the cored gallery, the two drilled core-access holes and their plugs from the A380 casting. Bolt in a two-piece stamped aluminium cold plate under the stack: a 3003-series pressed base with formed channels closed by a stamped cover, joined by fluxless vacuum brazing for non-ionic coolant compatibility, which is the construction Dana publishes for mounting hard-can modules. Hydroformed plate is the route most preferred in automotive because it balances cost against mechanical strength at volume; friction stir welding is available where higher running pressure is needed, and machined plate only for prototypes. Retain the ports on the plate, not the casting.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: A380 is a high-pressure die casting alloy and HPDC entrains gas, so a pressure-tight gallery inside it needs vacuum die casting plus vacuum impregnation, and still generates leak-test scrap at the 0.5 to 1.0 MPa air or helium test. Moving the coolant into a purpose-made brazed plate removes, in order of size: the vacuum impregnation at £1.20, the cores and their die complexity, the two core plugs at £0.70, the drilled access machining, and the leak-test fallout on a part that also carries the whole structural duty. Scrapping a leaking casting scraps 2.70 kg of machined aluminium; scrapping a leaking cold plate scraps a stamping. That asymmetry is the real mechanism. The functions this idea targets carry a combined value gap of £12.84 at Stage 3, against an affected component cost of £22.65; the saving claimed here is capped at that gap when the register is totalled.
ideaData.riskNotes: One part and one bolted, sealed interface are added where none existed, and that interface becomes a new leak path in exactly the position where a leak reaches the cells. Thermal resistance rises because there are now two interfaces (adhesive to plate, plate to casting or plate to cells) instead of one continuous wall, which works against DO-05's 5 degC spread. Pack height grows by the plate thickness, which the 12 kg net weight and the loadspace floor both have to absorb. Valeo's published position is that coolers are integrated inside the pack specifically to mitigate leakage risk, which is an argument against adding a separable joint.
ideaData.validationRequired: Helium leak test at 0.5 to 1.0 MPa on both constructions, run to statistical failure rate rather than to a pass. Thermal resistance measurement across the added interface at the design heat flux. Vibration test of the bolted plate joint to the vehicle schedule. Then a scrap-cost model comparing a leaking casting against a leaking plate at the measured failure rates.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Dana battery cold plate: lightweight stamped aluminium, fluxless brazed for non-ionic coolant compatibility, flow balanced for uniform pack temperature, for mounting hard-can modules (dana.com). Hydroformed cooling plates are the type most preferred in the automotive industry, suitable for mass production and balanced between cost and mechanical strength; FSW plates are used where running pressure is higher; machined plates are for prototypes (XD Thermal). Valeo integrates coolers inside the pack to mitigate leakage risk (valeo.com, 2 Sep 2024). A380 needs vacuum casting and a 0.5 to 1.0 MPa air or helium leak test to reach pressure tightness (casting-yz.com, 10 Nov 2025).
ideaData.investmentText: Cold plate stamping and brazing tooling plus a revised casting die, of the order of 240k GBP.

title: Control casting floor flatness to cut the thermal interface material volume, following Valeo's published practice

ideaData.title: Control casting floor flatness to cut the thermal interface material volume, following Valeo's published practice
ideaData.studyDecisionReason: Selected. No conflict with any other selected idea and it won its position in the conflict graph.
ideaData.groups: E Housing and closure, F Thermal and coolant
ideaData.componentsAffected: Thermal conductive adhesive; Housing, A380 die casting
ideaData.targetFunctions: Transfer heat; Support mass; Contain liquid; Exclude water; Transfer load; Contain debris; Control position
ideaData.technicalDescription: Machine or process-control the casting floor under the stack to a stated flatness, so the thermally conductive adhesive bond line falls from a gap-filling thickness set by worst-case casting variation to a controlled minimum. Valeo states it has developed a robust manufacturing process to hold best-in-class battery cooler flatness specifically to minimise the amount of thermal interface material. Pair it with locating the module on cast bosses referenced to the same machined datum, so the bond line is set by one feature rather than by a tolerance stack.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Thermally conductive gap filler is priced per kilogram and dispensed by volume, and the volume is set by the worst-case gap, not the average. Our current content is 0.42 kg at £3.78. Halving the design gap roughly halves the dispensed mass, about £1.70, and the thinner bond line also cuts thermal resistance, which is a second-order gain against DO-05's 55 degC and 5 degC spread. Because gas porosity reduces effective conductivity in proportion, tightening the casting process to control flatness usually improves conductivity at the same time. The functions this idea targets carry a combined value gap of £11.86 at Stage 3, against an affected component cost of £22.99; the saving claimed here is capped at that gap when the register is totalled.
ideaData.riskNotes: Flatness on a die casting is bought either with machining time or with tighter process control and higher scrap, and if the floor has to be machined the operation may cost more than the adhesive it saves. Too thin a bond line also loses compliance, so the adhesive must then absorb the differential expansion between the aluminium casting and the aluminium cell can across the temperature range, plus cell swelling through life, on a thinner section.
ideaData.validationRequired: Flatness capability study on the as-cast floor across a production sample, then a machined-floor comparison including cycle time and cost. Bond line thickness measurement by section on built packs. Thermal cycling and cell expansion cycling on the reduced bond line to confirm no loss of adhesion or shear retention. Thermal map across the stack against the 5 degC spread limit.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Valeo: battery coolers are built to best-in-class flatness specifically to minimise the amount of thermal interface material, and coolers are integrated inside the pack with a larger contact surface to the cells or modules as energy density and cooling density rise (valeo.com, 2 Sep 2024). Gas porosity reduces effective thermal conductivity proportionally (EMP Tech, Sep 2026).
ideaData.investmentText: Machining fixture or process capability work, of the order of 70k GBP.
ideaData.savingBasis: part-specific band, deep-dive

costSavingPotential.perVehicle: £1.63 to £1.87 per pack (review-corrected; study claimed £4.60 to £8.74 per pack)
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Review-corrected: Only the thermal conductive adhesive line falls (Parts #48: 0.42 kg, £3.78, i.e. £9.00/kg). The housing does not fall - it gains a flatness operation - so it is removed from the saving and enters only as an added cost. Adhesive saved uses the idea's own mechanism text: low £1.70 (its stated figure), high 50% of £3.78 = £1.89 ('halving the design gap roughly halves the dispensed mass'). Plausibility check on the starting bond line: 0.42 kg at 3.0 g/cc (Bergquist TGF 3010APS) = 140 cc spread over at most the 668 cm2 internal floor (Derivations r15 envelope 390 x 180 mm less 3.0 mm walls) gives an average >= 2.1 mm, so halving to ~1.05 mm is physically reachable; a 0.5 mm floor would be the ceiling at £2.88, not booked. Added cost: face-milling the floor, priced as cut time only, assuming it rides in the housing's existing machining setup (Rate_Card r13 HPDC rate already includes machining of sealing faces): 3 passes x 484 mm = 1,452 mm at 12,800-20,000 mm/min (Tungaloy die-cast examples) = 0.073-0.113 min at USD 20-50/hr (China 3-axis) x 0.79 = £0.02-£0.07/pack. Corrected = £1.70 - £0.07 = £1.63 to £1.89 - £0.02 = £1.87, within the £3.78 bound. Non-cutting time (tool change, any extra setup) and the scrap cost of the process-control route are NOT priced. ideaData.reviewOpenPoints: [CORRECTED 13 Oct 2026] ID-011 saves thermal adhesive only; the housing it also counted gets dearer, not cheaper. On the study's own £3.78 adhesive line and the idea's own 'halving' arithmetic, less a priced face-milling cut, the saving is £1.63-£1.87 per pack (£1.38-£1.59 risk-adjusted, about £166k-£191k a year), not £4.60-£8.74. It is still worth doing at £70k NRE (payback ~0.4 yr), and ID-001 must be put in conflict with it because both claim the same adhesive. ¶ [CRITICAL · quality] The claimed saving is larger than the only cost line that actually falls. This is the top-ranked Develop idea (weighted 4.73). It saves thermal adhesive: the content is £3.78, and the mechanism's own arithmetic is 'about £1.70'. The band of £4.60-£8.74 (risk-adjusted £3.91-£7.43) is reached only by counting the £19.21 A380 housing in the affected cost. But the idea makes the housing MORE expensive (flatness control or machining, which the risk text acknowledges). The high case is 2.3x the entire adhesive line and 5x the stated mechanism. Evidence: Parts: Thermal conductive adhesive 0.42 kg £3.78; Housing A380 £19.21. ID-011 Mechanism: 'Halving the design gap roughly halves the dispensed mass, about £1.70'. Risk: 'if the floor has to be machined the operation may cost more than the adhesive it saves'. Saving low/high 4.598/8.7362 on affected £22.99. Recommendation: Show the saving as unverified or overstated in front of the Director. The study's own deck (slide 4) warns that the bands are overstated. Do not quote £4.60-£8.74 per pack or the implied £0.55M-£1.05M a year. ¶ [MINOR · benchmark] The Valeo benchmark is confirmed, but it applies to a different kind of part. The Valeo source is a large EV battery cold plate (2000 x 1500 mm, flatness under 0.5 mm, glued into the pack), not the as-cast floor of an HPDC housing. It supports the principle, not the cost or feasibility of controlling flatness on an A380 die casting. Evidence: https://www.valeo.com/en/catalogue/ths/large-battery-liquid-cooler-for-ev/ Recommendation: Present it as a principle reference only.

ideaData.benchmarkReference: Silica aerogel at 0.013 to 0.020 W/m.K, 3 to 5 mm equivalent to 15 to 20 mm of conventional material; 1 to 2 mm sheets shown to suppress propagation (ScienceDirect, 19 Apr 2024 and 17 Jul 2024).

ideaData.title: Cut the plating specification to the minimum the joint needs
ideaData.studyDecisionReason: Selected. No conflict with any other selected idea and it won its position in the conflict graph.
ideaData.targetFunctions: Conduct current
ideaData.technicalDescription: Reduce plating thickness, or move from a full nickel plate to a selective plate only at the weld and contact areas.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Plating is priced by area and thickness. Most of a busbar's surface never carries a joint or sees a corrosive path, so plating it is paying for nothing. The functions this idea targets carry a combined value gap of £4.16 at Stage 3, against an affected component cost of £5.26; the saving claimed here is capped at that gap when the register is totalled.
ideaData.riskNotes: Nickel plating is what holds a stable low resistance across thousands of thermal cycles, and selective plating leaves bare copper that oxidises inside a sealed but humid enclosure.
ideaData.validationRequired: Joint resistance after humidity and thermal cycling on selectively plated samples.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Nickel-plated copper is the most common busbar choice for lithium packs because the nickel resists corrosion and holds stable resistance across thousands of thermal cycles (SunLith Energy, 15 Jul 2026).

ideaData.technicalDescription: Tender on a functional specification — 12 series channels, balancing current, communication protocol, ASIL level, operating window — rather than on the incumbent's schematic. In parallel, build a device-level should-cost from the published silicon: one 12S monitor (TI BQ79612-Q1, NXP MC33772 pairing or ADI LTC6811-1), one automotive microcontroller, one system basis chip, the passives, the bare board and the assembly. That gives a number to negotiate against rather than a price to accept.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: At £40.00 the BMS is 16.5 per cent of the bill of materials, the second largest line, and the only major figure in this study that is a stated price rather than a derivation. Four of the six worst value indices in the whole study — Balance voltage 3.33, Monitor voltage 2.10, Measure current 2.08, Exclude moisture 2.03 — are board area allocated from this one number. If the £40 is right, this is the worst-value item in the pack. If it is high, four of those indices evaporate. Either way the tender resolves it, which no other action in the register does. The functions this idea targets carry a combined value gap of £25.63 at Stage 3, against an affected component cost of £40.00; the saving claimed here is capped at that gap when the register is totalled.
ideaData.riskNotes: Requalifying a safety-related item is slow and expensive, and the incumbent's software may not port. A tender that only produces a benchmark price and no award still has value, but it consumes supplier goodwill. There is also a scope question that must be settled first: whether the £40 covers the printed circuit assembly alone or the whole electronics group, because the two readings differ by £9.48 and change the component count from 55 to 44.
ideaData.validationRequired: Three quotations at equal functional specification. A device-level should-cost built from published silicon prices to test them. Resolution of the £40 scope question against the supplier's own bill of materials before any comparison is drawn.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: NXP publishes a scalable portfolio with a named 48V mild hybrid tier built on MC33771, MC33772 and MC33664, which establishes that standard silicon exists for exactly this application rather than a bespoke design being necessary (NXP BMS solution deck). ideaData.title: Collapse monitoring, balancing, current sense and second-level protection into one 12S automotive front end
ideaData.studyDecisionReason: Selected. No conflict with any other selected idea and it won its position in the conflict graph.
ideaData.targetFunctions: Monitor voltage; Balance voltage; Transmit data; Exclude moisture; Measure current; Sense temperature
ideaData.technicalDescription: Specify a single 12-series cell monitor sized exactly to the string. Three named candidates: TI **BQ79612-Q1**, the 12S member of a family that is pin-to-pin compatible with the 14S BQ79614-Q1 and 16S BQ79616-Q1, with autonomous internal balancing that pauses and resumes on a programmable thermistor or die-temperature threshold above 105 degC, integrated post-ADC low-pass filters for state-of-charge, shunt current detection on the same device, and a hardware OVUV and OTUT comparator that acts as a second-level protector independently of the ADC. NXP **MC33771** (14 channels) or **MC33772** (6 channels), quoted at 0.8 mV cell voltage accuracy with integrated current sense and integrated 300 mA cell balancing, and positioned by NXP explicitly at the 48V mild hybrid tier. Analog Devices **LTC6811-1**, 12 cells, 290 microseconds, total measurement error under 1.2 mV.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: This is not one idea but four deletions on one device. The **balancing** function, allocated £8.00 at Stage 2 with a value index of 3.33 — the worst in the study — is external resistors and switches today; integrated 300 mA balancing removes them from the board entirely. The **current sense** chain, £5.40 allocated, folds into the same device's shunt detection, taking with it part of the analogue chain and possibly the separate amplifier. The **second-level protector**, normally a separate comparator or supervisor, is on-die as a hardware OVUV/OTUT comparator independent of the ADC, which is exactly the independence a functional safety case asks for. And **channel count** matches the string, so no silicon is bought unused. Board area, component count and placement time all fall together. The functions this idea targets carry a combined value gap of £25.63 at Stage 3, against an affected component cost of £40.00; the saving claimed here is capped at that gap when the register is totalled.
ideaData.riskNotes: Choosing a 12S device fixes the string at twelve cells, which voids the LFP idea at 14S and the 12S2P parallel-string idea at the same time — recorded as a conflict. Autonomous balancing running without microcontroller interaction is convenient but it removes a supervision point. Integrated current sense on the monitor puts measurement and protection on one die, which weakens the independence argument for ASIL B even while the hardware comparator strengthens it, so the safety case must be argued both ways. The TI family's pin compatibility partly mitigates the string lock-in, since a later move to 14S is a device swap rather than a redesign.
ideaData.validationRequired: Cell voltage accuracy against the state-of-charge estimator's error budget across the operating window. ASIL B decomposition demonstrating that the on-die hardware comparator provides adequate independence from the ADC path. Balancing current and thermal behaviour at the 105 degC pause threshold under the hot-country duty cycle. Shunt current accuracy at low current for key-off charge integration.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: TI BQ79612-Q1 / BQ79614-Q1 / BQ79616-Q1: 12S, 14S and 16S in one pin-compatible family, high-accuracy measurement in under 200 microseconds, autonomous balancing with programmable thermal pause above 105 degC, hardware OVUV and OTUT comparators as a second-level protector independent of the ADC, shunt current detection (ti.com BQ79616 datasheet; Würth Elektronik reference design page). NXP MC33771 and MC33772: 0.8 mV cell voltage accuracy, integrated current sense, integrated 300 mA cell balancing, ASIL-D power management, positioned by NXP at the 48V mild hybrid tier alongside MC33664 (NXP BMS solution deck). ADI LTC6811-1: 12 cells in 290 microseconds, total error under 1.2 mV.
ideaData.investmentText: Board redesign and safety rework, of the order of 400k GBP.
ideaData.savingBasis: part-specific band, deep-dive
ideaData.nreNote: Marginal share only. The full Electronics NRE investment is carried by ID-063; summing full NRE on every idea would overstate investment badly.

title: Move the housing to a glass-filled thermoplastic and transfer the thermal duty out of it

ideaData.title: Move the housing to a glass-filled thermoplastic and transfer the thermal duty out of it
ideaData.studyDecisionReason: Selected. No conflict with any other selected idea and it won its position in the conflict graph.
ideaData.targetFunctions: Support mass; Transfer heat; Contain liquid; Exclude water; Transfer load; Contain debris
ideaData.technicalDescription: Replace the A380 casting with an injection-moulded housing in a 30 to 50 per cent glass-filled polyamide or polypropylene, with the coolant duty moved to a separate brazed cold plate and the structural duty shared with a local metal insert at the mounting feet. Bosch's 48V pack is the production precedent: a plastic housing that protects against external damage while withstanding the continual expansion and contraction of the cells through service life, which means the moulding is also doing the module frame's job.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Three savings compound. Material: 2.70 kg of aluminium at £1.59/kg charged mass plus £5.00/kg conversion, about £18.01, becomes roughly 1.3 kg of filled polymer at a moulded cost typically a third to a half of the cast part. Process: no vacuum impregnation, no gallery cores, no core plugs, no structural leak test, no corrosion coating and no flange machining, because a moulded flange comes off the tool to size. Mass: roughly 1.4 kg out of a pack whose 12 kg stated weight the model currently overshoots by 0.876 kg, which is the only idea in the register that helps the mass reconciliation rather than hurting it. The functions this idea targets carry a combined value gap of £11.86 at Stage 3, against an affected component cost of £19.21; the saving claimed here is capped at that gap when the register is totalled.
ideaData.riskNotes: A polymer housing cannot be the heat path, so this idea is void unless it is taken with either the cold plate or the passive cooling idea. Creep under permanent stack preload at 85 degC becomes a design case aluminium never had, and glass-filled polyamide absorbs moisture, which moves dimensions in a sealed but humid enclosure. Fire performance in a cell event has to be demonstrated rather than assumed, which on an NMC pack reaching around 1000 degC is a serious question. Crash and mounting loads need local metal reinforcement at the feet.
ideaData.validationRequired: Creep and stress relaxation under stack preload at 85 degC for programme life. Flame test to the vehicle standard with a cell venting directly at the wall. Moisture conditioning and dimensional check at the sealing flange. Crash load analysis at the reinforced feet. Thermal path study confirming the pack meets DO-05 with the wall removed from the heat path.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Bosch 48V MHEV pack: plastic housing that protects against external damage while withstanding the continual expansion and contraction of the cells throughout service life, on a pack that uses passive cooling only (automotive-iq.com, 23 Aug 2024; chargedevs.com, 6 Nov 2017).
ideaData.investmentText: Injection tool of the order of 250k GBP plus the cold plate tooling if taken together.
ideaData.savingBasis: part-specific band, deep-dive
ideaData.nreNote: Marginal share only. The full Moulding tooling investment is carried by ID-064; summing full NRE on every idea would overstate investment badly.

title: Change the housing alloy from A380 to A413, A360, Silafont-36 or Castasil-37, selected on pressure tightness and conductivity together

ideaData.title: Change the housing alloy from A380 to A413, A360, Silafont-36 or Castasil-37, selected on pressure tightness and conductivity together
ideaData.studyDecisionReason: Mutually exclusive with a higher scoring idea already selected: ID-092.
ideaData.targetFunctions: Support mass; Transfer heat; Contain liquid; Exclude water; Transfer load; Contain debris
ideaData.technicalDescription: Four named candidates, in ascending order of capability and cost. **A360** (AlSi10Mg, <0.6 per cent Cu) gives a 10 to 15 per cent conductivity gain over A380 at similar mechanical properties, and its low copper removes the galvanic driver that makes the protective coating necessary at all. **A413** (AlSi12) is the direct answer to this pack's problem: it is specifically noted for excellent pressure tightness together with good thermal conductivity, which is exactly the pair of duties a cast coolant gallery needs. **Silafont-36** (AlSi10Mg, Rheinfelden, AA 365.0) reaches 130 to 150 W/m.K after T6, a 35 to 55 per cent improvement over ADC12, and is described as the workhorse alloy for EV thermal management housings. **Castasil-37** reaches 139 to 173 W/m.K, the highest of any commercially die-castable AlSi alloy, at roughly 75 per cent of pure aluminium, and needs no heat treatment, which avoids the distortion a T6 quench would put into a sealing flange. Baseline A380/ADC12 sits at 96 to 98 W/m.K.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Three cost mechanisms, not one. First, conductivity: at 96 W/m.K the A380 wall is the thermal bottleneck between the adhesive and the coolant, so wall section is being carried for heat rather than for strength. Castasil-37 at up to 173 W/m.K is 1.8 times A380, which allows either a thinner base wall at constant thermal resistance or a smaller gallery footprint. On a 2.70 kg casting, a 15 per cent section reduction in the base is roughly 0.25 kg of aluminium at £1.59/kg plus its share of the £5.00/kg conversion, about £1.65. Second, porosity: gas porosity reduces effective thermal conductivity in proportion, so an alloy that needs less vacuum assistance to reach a given leak rate delivers its published conductivity rather than a derated one. Third, and largest, A360 and A413 both carry far less copper than A380, which removes the corrosion driver and puts the £0.70 coating line in play as a deletion rather than a reduction. The functions this idea targets carry a combined value gap of £11.86 at Stage 3, against an affected component cost of £19.21; the saving claimed here is capped at that gap when the register is totalled.
ideaData.riskNotes: The AlSi10MnMg structural family (Silafont-36, Castasil-37, Aural-2) is built around ultra-low iron below 0.15 per cent, which raises die soldering risk and demands tighter process control and more expensive ingot. Silafont-36 needs a T6 to reach its quoted conductivity, and a T6 quench on a part with a machined sealing flange and two port faces will distort them; Castasil-37 avoids that but its lower silicon makes filling a thin cored section harder, which is the opposite of what a coolant gallery wants. A413's high silicon costs machinability, and this housing has a flange, two ports and a disconnect pad to machine. A380's copper content is precisely why it machines well, so moving away from it adds machining cost that partly offsets the material and coating saving.
ideaData.validationRequired: Cast trial on each candidate measuring, in this order: helium leak rate at 0.5 to 1.0 MPa on the gallery, porosity by density and CT section, effective thermal conductivity on a cut sample rather than the published figure, machinability on the flange and port faces, and salt spray on the uncoated part to test whether the coating can be deleted. Then re-run the pack thermal model at the measured conductivity to find the real allowable wall reduction against DO-05.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Castasil-37: up to 173 W/m.K at operating temperature, the highest of any commercially die-castable AlSi alloy, about 75 per cent of pure aluminium (EMP Tech, Sep 2026). Silafont-36: 130 to 150 W/m.K after T6, 35 to 55 per cent above ADC12, described as the workhorse for EV thermal housings (same source). ADC12/A380: 96 to 98 W/m.K, suitable below 20 W/cm2 heat flux, which covers battery trays. A413: excellent pressure tightness and thermal conductivity, used where sealed housings and heat dissipation both matter (Amfas International, 26 Jan 2026). A360: 10 to 15 per cent conductivity gain over A380 with <0.6 per cent Cu for corrosion resistance (Cast-Mold, 3 Sep 2025). AlSi10MnMg family and its <0.15 per cent Fe: Transformación Puebla, 5 Mar 2026; NADCA 2021 Alloy Data.
ideaData.investmentText: Alloy trial and die adjustment, of the order of 120k GBP; a full die change if section is reduced.

ideaData.studyDecisionReason: Mutually exclusive with a higher scoring idea already selected: ID-144.
ideaData.targetFunctions: Exclude water; Contain debris; Prevent contact; Permit access
ideaData.technicalDescription: Replace PA66 GF30 with a filled polypropylene grade where the cover's duty is closure, sealing and touch protection rather than structure or heat.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Polypropylene resin costs roughly half of PA66 per kilogram, moulds at lower temperature with a shorter cycle, and absorbs almost no moisture, which removes the dimensional drift PA66 shows in a damp enclosure. The functions this idea targets carry a combined value gap of £1.81 at Stage 3, against an affected component cost of £3.95; the saving claimed here is capped at that gap when the register is totalled.
ideaData.riskNotes: PP is weaker and softer, so terminal stud retention and handle attachment both need review. Its temperature capability is lower, which matters directly above cells in a vent event.
ideaData.validationRequired: Terminal pull-out and handle load test in PP, and temperature capability check against the vent gas path.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: No published benchmark. No comparable public 48V pack design was found for this specific change.
ideaData.investmentText: Tool change, of the order of 60k GBP.
ideaData.savingBasis: part-specific band

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Study register band (part-specific band) on £3.95 affected cost = £0.99 to £1.58 per pack × 120,000 packs/yr (study volume, README). title: Mould the handles as features of the cover instead of separate parts

ideaData.title: Mould the handles as features of the cover instead of separate parts
ideaData.studyDecisionReason: Selected. No conflict with any other selected idea and it won its position in the conflict graph.
ideaData.componentsAffected: Top cover, PA66 GF30; Service handle
ideaData.targetFunctions: Exclude water; Carry mass; Contain debris; Prevent contact; Permit access
ideaData.technicalDescription: Form two integral grip features in the cover moulding rather than fitting two separate handles.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Two parts and two fitting operations disappear into a tool change on a part that already exists. There is nothing to come loose in service. The functions this idea targets carry a combined value gap of £1.81 at Stage 3, against an affected component cost of £5.25; the saving claimed here is capped at that gap when the register is totalled.

ideaData.validationRequired: Lift load test at twice pack mass through the integral grips, and a moulding trial for sink.

title: Move from a cure-in-place adhesive sealant to a formed-in-place foamed gasket

ideaData.title: Move from a cure-in-place adhesive sealant to a formed-in-place foamed gasket
ideaData.studyDecisionReason: Mutually exclusive with a higher scoring idea already selected: ID-100.
ideaData.targetFunctions: Prevent leakage
ideaData.technicalDescription: Replace the ITW HA1820 adhesive bead with a formed-in-place polyurethane gasket that seals without bonding.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: A foamed gasket uses far less material per metre than an adhesive bead and needs no cure oven. It also lets the cover be removed for service without cutting, which the adhesive does not. The functions this idea targets carry a combined value gap of £0.00 at Stage 3, against an affected component cost of £0.85; the saving claimed here is capped at that gap when the register is totalled.
ideaData.riskNotes: The sealant currently contributes to cover retention as well as sealing, so removing the bond means more fasteners. A foamed gasket also needs a groove in the flange, which is a tool change on both parts.
ideaData.validationRequired: IP67 verification with the gasket, and a cover retention check with the bond removed.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: No published benchmark. No comparable public 48V pack design was found for this specific change.
ideaData.investmentText: Dispense head and tool change, of the order of 70k GBP.

title: Reduce the bead section and the fastener count together by tightening flange flatness

ideaData.title: Reduce the bead section and the fastener count together by tightening flange flatness
ideaData.studyDecisionReason: Selected. No conflict with any other selected idea and it won its position in the conflict graph.
ideaData.componentsAffected: Sealant, ITW HA1820; Top cover fastener M5
ideaData.targetFunctions: Prevent leakage; Transmit force
ideaData.technicalDescription: Control flange flatness on both the casting and the cover so the sealant bead can be thinner and fewer screws are needed to close the joint.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Bead volume is set by the worst-case gap and screw count by the worst-case bow. Both fall directly with flatness, and they fall together because they are the same root cause. The functions this idea targets carry a combined value gap of £0.00 at Stage 3, against an affected component cost of £1.33; the saving claimed here is capped at that gap when the register is totalled.
ideaData.riskNotes: Flatness on a die casting is bought with machining, and on a moulding with cycle time and fixturing. If the flange must be machined the saving may reverse.
ideaData.validationRequired: Flange flatness capability study on both parts, then a leak test at reduced bead and screw count.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Valeo controls cooler flatness specifically to minimise thermal interface material quantity, the same tolerance-to-material mechanism (valeo.com, 2 Sep 2024).

title: Delete the protective coating by moving to a low-copper alloy rather than by accepting corrosion

ideaData.title: Delete the protective coating by moving to a low-copper alloy rather than by accepting corrosion
ideaData.studyDecisionReason: Selected. No conflict with any other selected idea and it won its position in the conflict graph.
ideaData.targetFunctions: Resist corrosion
ideaData.technicalDescription: Do not simply delete the coating from A380. A380 carries 3 to 4 per cent copper, and copper forms galvanic cells within the alloy's own microstructure that accelerate corrosion, which is why the coating is there. Instead move to A360 (<0.6 per cent Cu) or the AlSi10MnMg structural family (Silafont-36, Castasil-37, Aural-2), all of which are copper-free or near copper-free and are described as having improved corrosion resistance and weldability for that reason. Then delete the coating on the corrosion merit of the alloy.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: The coating at £0.70 exists to compensate for an alloy choice made for castability and machinability. Changing the alloy removes the cause rather than treating the symptom, which is the definition of attacking an unwanted function. Resist corrosion is classified unwanted at Stage 2 and carries £0.70; deleting the coating line entirely also removes a spray booth, its material, its cure and its masking of the sealing faces and coolant ports, none of which appears in the piece price but all of which appears in the supplier's cost. The functions this idea targets carry a combined value gap of £0.50 at Stage 3, against an affected component cost of £0.70; the saving claimed here is capped at that gap when the register is totalled.
ideaData.riskNotes: Low-copper alloys machine worse than A380 precisely because copper is what produces short brittle chips, and this housing has a sealing flange, two port faces and a mounting pad to machine. Ultra-low-iron grades also raise die soldering risk and ingot price. Cosmetic corrosion is still accepted in a wet under-floor position, which may be rejected on appearance even if function is unaffected.
ideaData.validationRequired: Salt spray to the vehicle standard on uncoated A360 and Castasil-37 samples, with particular attention to the sealing faces and the coolant port bores where corrosion product would break a seal. Machinability trial on the flange. Galvanic couple check at the steel fastener and the copper terminal interfaces.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: A360's low copper content below 0.6 per cent gives a significant corrosion advantage over A380, because copper creates galvanic cells within the microstructure; suited to outdoor enclosures and components exposed to road salt (Cast-Mold, 3 Sep 2025). The AlSi10MnMg family is copper-free, which improves corrosion resistance and weldability (Transformación Puebla, 5 Mar 2026). A380's copper is also what gives it good machinability (same source).
ideaData.investmentText: Alloy trial; no new tooling if section is unchanged.
ideaData.savingBasis: part-specific band, deep-dive
ideaData.nreNote: Marginal share only. The full Moulding tooling investment is carried by ID-064; summing full NRE on every idea would overstate investment badly.

ideaData.studyDecisionReason: Selected. No conflict with any other selected idea and its risk-adjusted saving of £4.03 is at or above 1 per cent of the bill of materials, so it is not excluded by falling below the generic score threshold.
ideaData.targetFunctions: Support mass; Transfer heat; Contain liquid; Exclude water; Transfer load; Contain debris
ideaData.technicalDescription: Restrict machining to the sealing flange, the coolant port faces and the disconnect mounting pad, leaving all other surfaces as cast.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Machining is charged by time and fixturing. Every face machined for tidiness rather than function is paid for on 840,000 parts. Casting to size also avoids a second fixturing operation. The functions this idea targets carry a combined value gap of £11.86 at Stage 3, against an affected component cost of £19.21; the saving claimed here is capped at that gap when the register is totalled.
ideaData.riskNotes: As-cast surfaces carry draft and flash, which affects anything that has to seal or locate against them, and they look worse if any face is visible. Datum strategy must be built around the few machined faces.
ideaData.validationRequired: Datum and tolerance study identifying which faces genuinely need machining, then a fixturing plan on the reduced set.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: No published benchmark. No comparable public 48V pack design was found for this specific change.
ideaData.savingBasis: class default band, no part-specific estimate made

title: Break the pack into separately sourced content instead of a single turnkey supply

ideaData.title: Break the pack into separately sourced content instead of a single turnkey supply
ideaData.studyDecisionReason: Selected. No conflict with any other selected idea and it won its position in the conflict graph.
ideaData.groups: A Cell stack, D Electronics and protection, E Housing and closure
ideaData.componentsAffected: NMC prismatic cell; BMS printed circuit assembly; Housing, A380 die casting
ideaData.targetFunctions: Store energy; Deliver power; Accept charge; Monitor voltage; Balance voltage; Deliver current; Transmit data; Exclude moisture; Support mass; Transfer heat; Measure current; Sense temperature; Contain liquid; Exclude water; Transfer load; Contain debris
ideaData.technicalDescription: Buy the cells, the electronics and the housing on separate contracts and have the pack assembled to our own design, rather than buying a complete pack from one supplier.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: A turnkey supplier applies its own margin and overhead across content it buys in, including the electronics and the casting. Contracting each directly removes one layer of margin from roughly half the bill of materials. The functions this idea targets carry a combined value gap of £75.89 at Stage 3, against an affected component cost of £181.62; the saving claimed here is capped at that gap when the register is totalled.
ideaData.riskNotes: The integration risk, the warranty and the functional safety case all move in-house, which is a substantial capability commitment. A single supplier who owns the whole pack is also easier to hold to a performance guarantee.
ideaData.validationRequired: Compare a turnkey quotation against the sum of directly contracted content plus our own integration cost, including warranty provision.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: No published benchmark. No comparable public 48V pack design was found for this specific change.
ideaData.savingBasis: class default band, no part-specific estimate made

costSavingPotential.perVehicle: Not booked — ceiling £4.25–£8.08 per pack; OEM integration, safety-case and warranty costs are unpriced (review-corrected; study claimed £27.24 to £54.49 per pack)

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Review-corrected: De-bundling removes margin, not part cost, so the ceiling is the margin the study's own cascade puts on the content being moved. Summary_Assembly charges SG&A at 6% on supplier cost minus the cell (£259.33 - £122.41 = £136.91, giving £8.21). It charges profit at 6% on that base plus SG&A (£8.71), which is margin-on-margin. The cell carries no SG&A or profit, only a 1.5% handling charge (£1.84), because EVE makes both the cells and the pack and the cell price already includes the cell maker's margin. The total removable pool is therefore £18.76, not £27-£54. The idea moves the BMS (£40.00) and the housing (£19.21) out of the assembler's marked-up base. The margin on that £59.21 is £59.21 x (1.06 x 1.06 - 1) = £7.32. The rest of the bought-in parts and the assembly conversion stay with whoever assembles the pack and keep their margin. The low case assumes the assembler still charges the study's own 1.5% handling rate on directed BMS and housing (-£0.89) and that cell handling stays. The high case assumes the cell handling charge is also removed (+£1.84). Both cases then deduct the OEM's added purchasing cost on the £181.62 now contracted directly: 1.2% of spend (CAPS industrial-manufacturing average) in the low case and 0.59% (Hackett world class) in the high case, i.e. £2.18 / £1.07. The result is £4.25-£8.08/pack, within the £18.76 margin pool. Not booked: in-house integration engineering, the functional safety case, incoming quality and the warranty liability that moves to the OEM under a directed-buy arrangement have no cited public percentage and are not deducted. Together they could plausibly absorb the remainder. The figure is a ceiling to test with the idea's own validation step (turnkey quote against direct content plus integration cost). ideaData.reviewOpenPoints: [CORRECTED 13 Oct 2026] The £27-£54/pack claim exceeded the entire margin layer in the study's own cost build-up, which is £18.76: SG&A £8.21 + profit £8.71 + cell handling £1.84. The cells carry no pack-supplier margin because EVE makes both. Removing the margin on the directly sourced BMS and housing, net of the OEM's added purchasing cost, gives at most £4.25-£8.08/pack (£2.98-£5.66 risk-adjusted), before integration, safety-case and warranty costs that move in-house. Treat it as a ceiling to be tested by quotation, not a booked saving, and re-run the conflict with the BMS retender (ID-058), which now looks the stronger idea. ¶ [CRITICAL · quality] Over-claim on a Develop idea. 'Removes one layer of margin' is credited £27.24-£54.49/pack (risk-adjusted £19.07-£38.14). The study's own cascade carries only £8.21 SG&A + £8.71 profit on bought-in content and conversion plus a £1.84 cell handling charge (£18.76 total), and states the cell content already carries no pack-supplier SG&A or profit. The claimed saving exceeds the entire modelled margin layer. Evidence: Summary_Assembly: 'SG&A on bought-in and conversion 8.21 ... Cell content excluded from the base'; 'Profit on bought-in and conversion 8.71'; 'Cell handling charge 1.84'; 'EVE Energy manufactures both the cells and the pack. The cell price already carries a cell-maker's margin.' Saving basis: 'class default band'. Recommendation: Cap at the modelled margin actually removable (well under £18.76, net of in-house integration, warranty and safety-case cost the trade-offs list) and re-run the evaluation. ¶ [MINOR · quality] NRE £50,000 sits at/above the idea's own investment band 'Low, under 50k GBP'. Same placeholder on ID-136, 137, 140, 143, 144, 148, 149, 151. Evidence: Ideas ID-138 Investment 'Low, under 50k GBP'; Evaluation NRE GBP 50000. Recommendation: Replace the £50k placeholder with an estimate or label it as a placeholder.

reviewCorrection.riskAdjustedNote: NRE unchanged at the record's £50,000, but it is a placeholder: the idea's own investment band is 'Low, under 50k GBP', and it excludes building in-house pack integration and safety-case capability. Payback = 50,000 / (£2.98 x 120,000) = 0.14 yr. It is short only because the NRE is unpriced.
reviewCorrection.systemTradeNote: ID-138 currently wins C20 over ID-013 (dual-source the cell, risk-adjusted £3.43-£7.71) and C36 over ID-058 (BMS retender, deep-dive part-specific, £4.20-£8.40). Corrected, ID-138 at £2.98-£5.66 is below ID-058, and both ID-013 and ID-058 score higher on weighted score (4.80 and 4.47 against 3.93), so re-run the conflict graph. ID-058 attacks the BMS price directly and probably captures more than de-bundling its margin. De-bundling also moves warranty, the functional safety case and pack performance guarantees from EVE to the OEM. The study's warranty provision (£3.34, 1.2%) and the single-supplier performance guarantee are system-level costs this idea shifts rather than removes.
openQuestions: Would EVE quote a directed-buy or consigned arrangement, and at what handling fee on directed BMS and housing?
Who assembles the pack after de-bundling (EVE, a contract assembler or the OEM in-house), and what is the margin on conversion and the remaining £60.64 of bought-in parts?
Annual OEM cost for integration engineering, the functional safety case (ASIL), incoming quality and warranty self-insurance. This sets whether any net saving remains.
Is the 6% SG&A / 6% profit (Assumptions A-07, [Guessing]) the right rate for EVE? Roland Berger's China supplier EBIT is 5.7%.

evidenceSources.title: Supplier margins around 6% (the study's profit rate) are realistic
evidenceSources.supports: partly: Roland Berger/Lazard Global Automotive Supplier Study 2025: average supplier EBIT 4.7% in 2024 (5.3% in 2023); Chinese suppliers highest at 5.7%. The study's 6% is at or slightly above the benchmark, so the margin pool is if anything generous.

evidenceSources.title: OEM purchasing cost as a share of spend
evidenceSources.supports: supports: ISM citing Hackett (2016): average 0.72%, world class 0.59% of spend. CAPS Research (2014): industrial manufacturing 1.2%, overall average 1.2%. Dated, and covers purchasing only, not integration, quality or warranty.

evidenceSources.title: OEMs commonly source cells directly and use a third party for the rest (system integration model)
evidenceSources.supports: partly: S&P Global Mobility: the 'system integration' model, where the OEM manages supply of one or two components and a third party sources the rest, covers about 54% of battery GWh. The model is real, but no margin saving is quantified.

evidenceSources.title: Published tier-1 handling fee / markup on OEM-directed (directed-buy) parts
evidenceSources.supports: not found: No public figure found. An FGV paper on directed-buy agreements covers tier-1 liability limits for warranty and line stoppage on OEM-imposed tier-2s, which supports the point that liability moves to the OEM, but gives no fee.

evidenceSources.title: Consultancy (McKinsey/BCG/Bain/PwC) benchmark for margin stacking on bought-in cells in turnkey battery supply
evidenceSources.supports: not found: None found in the searches run. Roland Berger's battery-strategy piece discusses OEM dependency on cell makers but gives no margin-stack figure.

evidenceSources.title: Tier-1 retail-price-equivalent markup about 1.5x
evidenceSources.supports: contradicts: The National Academies figure covers vehicle-level indirect costs (OEM RPE), not tier-1 margin on bought-in content. Not used.

title: Index all copper content to LME and buy the metal separately from the conversion

ideaData.title: Index all copper content to LME and buy the metal separately from the conversion
ideaData.studyDecisionReason: Selected. No conflict with any other selected idea and its weighted score of 4.33 is at or above the 3.95 threshold.
ideaData.componentsAffected: Cell interconnect busbar, Cu T2Y; Sealing stud terminal, Cu T2Y; Flexible copper busbar, Cu T2Y2; Equipotential bonding strap; Busbar terminal bolt
ideaData.targetFunctions: Conduct current; Transfer current; Absorb expansion; Prevent leakage; Equalise potential; Transmit force
ideaData.technicalDescription: Split copper parts into a metal element indexed to LME and a conversion element fixed by contract, rather than a single price the supplier reprices annually.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Copper sits at or near a record. A single all-in price means the supplier carries metal risk and prices a premium for it, and that premium does not come back when the metal falls. The functions this idea targets carry a combined value gap of £5.16 at Stage 3, against an affected component cost of £10.84; the saving claimed here is capped at that gap when the register is totalled.
ideaData.riskNotes: Metal risk moves to us and there is no protection if copper rises further. Administering an indexed contract on several small parts costs more than it saves unless the copper content is material.
ideaData.validationRequired: Back-test the proposed index formula against 2024 to 2026 copper actuals, and compare against the supplier's fixed pricing history.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Copper at 6.55 USD per pound on 4 September 2026 is 14,440 USD per tonne, against an IMF LME spot average for 2026 of 12,842 (TradingEconomics; Cbonds).

title: Move from laser welding to ultrasonic welding at the cell terminals

ideaData.title: Move from laser welding to ultrasonic welding at the cell terminals
ideaData.studyDecisionReason: Selected. No conflict with any other selected idea and it won its position in the conflict graph.
ideaData.groups: A Cell stack, C Electrical interconnect, D Electronics and protection
ideaData.componentsAffected: NMC prismatic cell; Cell interconnect busbar, Cu T2Y; Cell contacting system; NTC thermistor
ideaData.targetFunctions: Store energy; Deliver power; Accept charge; Deliver current; Conduct current; Monitor voltage; Sense temperature
ideaData.technicalDescription: Weld busbars to cell terminals ultrasonically rather than by laser, which also opens the door to aluminium busbars.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Ultrasonic welding does not melt the metal, so it avoids the weld depth control problem that makes laser welding onto a cell terminal risky, and it tolerates the oxide layer that makes aluminium hard to laser weld. The functions this idea targets carry a combined value gap of £53.35 at Stage 3, against an affected component cost of £131.83; the saving claimed here is capped at that gap when the register is totalled.
ideaData.riskNotes: Ultrasonic welding applies mechanical load to the cell terminal, which prismatic cells tolerate less well than a laser process, and joint area is limited by the sonotrode. Cycle time for 26 joints may be worse.
ideaData.validationRequired: Joint strength and resistance comparison, plus a cell terminal load check during welding.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Ultrasonic welding, which does not melt the metal, pairs well with aluminium busbars; laser weld depth control is critical because excessive penetration can damage the cell (SunLith Energy, 15 Jul 2026; Joining Technologies).
ideaData.investmentText: Ultrasonic station, of the order of 150k GBP.
ideaData.conflictsWith: C26, C37 · Review-added conflicts: ID-150 vs ID-008: ID-008 already specifies the laser-to-ultrasonic switch together with aluminium busbars. Both cannot be credited, so add ID-150 to set C6 or mark it as absorbed by ID-008.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Review-corrected: A joining-process change can only save on the joining step, so the affected cost is the study's laser-welding step: Conversion row 6, 26 joints, 3 min, machine £1.10 (£22/hr) + labour £0.26 (Rate_Card row 16, £5.20/hr) = £1.36/pack. The ultrasonic step was costed with the study's own rates: (i) cycle time = the study's 3 min plus 0.4-0.9 s more weld time per joint x 26 joints. That is the gap between published ultrasonic weld times of 0.5-1.0 s (Laserax; LEONI/Telsonic busbar line about 0.9 s) and laser at under 0.1 s. Handling and clamping are assumed equal. (ii) Machine rate = £22/hr x a capex ratio: 0.36 in the best case (lowest ultrasonic list price $18k against the 'from $50k' laser entry price, Assembly Magazine) and 1.0 in the worst case. The worst case reflects the idea's own £150k ultrasonic-station estimate and Manz's statement only that laser costs more to buy. (iii) Labour at £5.20/hr x cycle. (iv) Sonotrode wear, which a laser does not have: $2k-5k per sonotrode per about 70,000 copper welds (EWI) x 26 joints x 0.79 = £0.59-£1.47/pack. The anvil is excluded, which flatters ultrasonic. The ultrasonic step comes out at £1.28-£3.00 against £1.36 for laser, a change of +£0.08 to -£1.64/pack, so the best case is bounded by and almost equal to the laser step. Beyond the arithmetic, the cell is a prismatic hard-can format. Ultrasonic welding is mainly a pouch-tab process because its vibration and clamping pressure can damage prismatic and cylindrical cells, and the study's own risk note says the same. Not booked: the idea is a probable cost increase and a cell-damage risk. Any aluminium-busbar benefit belongs to ID-008, which already includes the switch to ultrasonic welding. Fed through the study's cascade (burden 60%, scrap 1.8%, SG&A 6%, profit 6%, x1.83), the delivered-price effect would be +£0.14 to -£3.01.
