ideaData.reviewOpenPoints: [CORRECTED 13 Oct 2026] The £19.77-£39.55/pack claim priced the cell, not the weld. The whole laser-welding step in the study costs £1.36/pack. Re-costed with the study's own rates and published cycle-time and tool-wear data, ultrasonic welding runs from £0.08/pack cheaper to £1.64/pack dearer, and the process is generally avoided on prismatic hard-can cells because of terminal damage risk. Recommend withdrawing ID-150 from the Develop list and the Director deck. ¶ [CRITICAL · quality] Over-claim on a Develop idea. A weld-process change is credited £19.77-£39.55/pack (risk-adjusted £13.84-£27.68, ~£1.7-3.3M/yr) because the class-default 15-30% band was applied to an affected cost of £131.83 that is 93% the cell (£122.41). The study's own Conversion sheet prices the entire laser-welding step at £1.36/pack, and the non-cell parts touched total £9.42. Evidence: Conversion: 'Laser welding, 26 joints | 3 min | £22/hr | machine £1.10 | labour £0.26'. Parts: cell £122.41, busbars £5.26, contacting system £3.80, NTC £0.36. Ideas ID-150 Saving basis: 'class default band, no part-specific estimate made'. Deck slide 82: class-default bands are 'almost all on parts below half a per cent of the bill of materials'. Recommendation: Re-estimate on the weld step and busbar content only (order of £1-2/pack before any Al-busbar benefit, which belongs to ID-008); remove the cell from the affected cost; withdraw the current figure from the Director deck.

reviewCorrection.riskAdjustedNote: NRE unchanged at the record's £150,000 (ultrasonic station). The risk-adjusted low case is negative, so the idea never pays back. Even the high case (£0.06/pack x 120,000 = about £6.6k/yr) would take about 23 years, against a 7-year programme. p 0.7 is kept as recorded, but it looks optimistic for a prismatic hard-can terminal.
reviewCorrection.systemTradeNote: ID-150 currently displaces ID-054 (C26) and ID-135 (C37). With the corrected saving below 0.2% of the BOM, its saving-potential score falls from 5 to 1 (Evaluation scoring rule), and the conflict graph should be re-run. Do not let ID-135 inherit the slot unexamined: its £12.24-£26.93 is also a class-default band on the £122.41 cell and needs the same re-estimate. Changing the weld process also touches the cell supplier's terminal design and validation (terminal load, joint resistance over thermal cycling), so the trade is pack-level, not just a line change.
openQuestions: Is the cell terminal design (EVE M41-type prismatic, Al/Cu terminals) qualified by the cell maker for ultrasonic welding at all?
Does the £22/hr laser machine rate already include laser consumables (cover glass, gas, power)? If not, the laser step is understated slightly.
Busbar thickness: at or over 3 mm Cu, published guidance favours laser.
Actual ultrasonic station capex for 26 joints at a 3 min takt; the record's £150k is not sourced.

evidenceSources.title: Ultrasonic welding suits pouch tabs; laser is the norm for prismatic/cylindrical terminals
evidenceSources.supports: supports: Trade press states ultrasonic welding is mostly useful for pouch cells because shocks and pressure can damage cylindrical or prismatic cells. Laser welds busbars directly to cylindrical cells.

evidenceSources.title: No single tab-to-busbar process is universally superior; ultrasonic is sensitive to thickness, stack geometry and tool wear
evidenceSources.supports: partly: A Micromachines (Dec 2025) open-access review of resistance, laser and ultrasonic tab-to-busbar welding. Read from the abstract via search only; the full text was blocked by the egress proxy.

evidenceSources.title: Ultrasonic weld time 0.5-1.0 s per joint against laser under 0.1 s
evidenceSources.supports: partly: Laserax (a laser vendor, so biased) says ultrasonic wire bonding takes 500-1000 ms per weld and its laser averages under 100 ms per cell including movement.

evidenceSources.title: Production ultrasonic busbar weld cycle about 0.9 s
evidenceSources.supports: partly: LEONI's line for Jaguar uses Telsonic Soniqtwist torsional welding on an aluminium busbar, with a weld cycle of about 0.9 s. This is a busbar-to-sleeve joint, not a cell terminal.

evidenceSources.title: Ultrasonic equipment costs less than laser
evidenceSources.supports: partly: Assembly Magazine: ultrasonic welders $18k-45k against laser 'from $50k' (general-purpose machines, undated). Manz: laser acquisition costs are higher than ultrasonic but operating costs are lower.

evidenceSources.title: Sonotrode wear is a per-weld consumable
evidenceSources.supports: supports: EWI: tool-steel sonotrodes last about 70,000 welds in copper ultrasonic metal welding and cost about $2k-5k each; high-volume battery plants spend $0.5M-2M a year on sonotrodes.

evidenceSources.title: Ultrasonic suits thin busbars and aluminium; laser suits thicker copper
evidenceSources.supports: partly: SunLith Energy (cited by the study itself): under about 3 mm favours ultrasonic, over 3 mm favours laser or resistance welding, and aluminium oxide favours a non-melting process. Seen via search snippet only.

evidenceSources.title: Torsional ultrasonic welding reduces the load on prismatic cell terminals
evidenceSources.supports: not found: No published terminal-load or process-window data were found for prismatic cell terminals; the material available is vendor marketing only.
